object_description: two offset compact two-story volumes framing connected outdoor squares
design_condition: Two compact volumes are moved away from the waterfront and offset to align with existing utility buildings, forming a permeable sequence of outdoor squares and opening the entire lakeshore.

positive.statement: The precise urban development creates great spatial potential in interaction with the existing building.
The offset positioning creates well-sized outdoor spaces and a balanced sequence of small squares.
The complex has spatial permeability along the diagonals and allows visual references to the lake and garden.
The operational organization and development are clear and plausible.
The building volumes and outdoor spaces are harmoniously proportioned and dimensioned.
The opening to the lake and the sequence of spaces are very much appreciated.

negative.statement: Several required additional rooms are missing and the gymnasium dimensions are too small.
The access areas inside the two buildings appear rather oversized.
The buildings should manifest themselves in a more architecturally conscious and decisive manner.
The formal formulation appears somewhat anemic and is unable to create atmospheric quality.
The outdoor area is treated only schematically, without sufficient information about planting, topography, or retreat areas.
The continuous mineral arrival area lacks water, furniture, and trees.
